card.occupation: Full-time student, BSc Construction Management at the University of Reading (second year). Previously worked six years as a shift team leader at a distribution warehouse near Theale. He keeps a few weekend shifts there over the summer.
card.education_detail: Finished technical secondary school (technikum) in Poland with a qualification in building technology. In the UK he did a forklift licence, an Access to HE course and a Level 3 in supervisory management through work. He started his degree at 31 with a student loan and savings.
card.household: Lives with his wife Agnieszka (32), a dental nurse at a practice in Wokingham, in a rented two-bedroom flat in Earley. The second bedroom is his study room. They have no children yet, though they have talked about it for after he graduates.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Rzeszów, south-east Poland. He moved to the UK at 19 to join an older cousin in Reading and has stayed since. He is Roman Catholic and goes to Mass at the Polish church in Reading most Sundays, more from habit and family expectation than strong feeling. He speaks Polish at home and with family, and English everywhere else. He has pre-settled-then-settled status and has not bothered with citizenship yet, though he says he will 'when there is time'.
card.professional_persona: Organised and exact. At the warehouse he was known for keeping a tight rota and not tolerating excuses. At university he submits work early, keeps a spreadsheet of every deadline and finds group projects frustrating when others are vague. He wants clear briefs and measurable results, and he is not interested in networking events.
card.sports_persona: Runs 5k three mornings a week on a fixed route around Maiden Erlegh Lake and records times on a watch. He watches Ekstraklasa and Premier League football results rather than full matches, and has a casual attachment to Stal Rzeszów. He does not play team sports any more.
card.arts_persona: Not much interest. He watches the occasional action film or a Polish crime series with Agnieszka and listens to the radio in the car. He has not been to a gallery or the theatre in years and sees little point in it.
card.travel_persona: Travels to Poland twice a year, at Christmas and in summer, usually by flying from Luton or Stansted to Rzeszów. He prefers going back to the same places and once did a week in Croatia because Agnieszka wanted it. He books early, compares prices carefully and dislikes disorganised trips.
card.culinary_persona: Eats simply and regularly. Agnieszka cooks more Polish food at weekends, such as pierogi and żurek at Easter. On weekdays he cooks chicken, rice and vegetables in batches. He shops at Lidl and the Polish shop on Oxford Road, drinks black coffee, and has a beer occasionally but not much.
hobbies_and_interests: Fixing and maintaining his Skoda Octavia himself
Watching construction and engineering videos on YouTube
skills: Excel, including pivot tables and budgeting
Basic AutoCAD and quantity take-off from drawings
card.career_goals: Graduate in 2026 and get onto a site manager or assistant project manager graduate scheme with a mid-size contractor in the Thames Valley. Long term he wants to become chartered with CIOB and earn enough to buy a house in Woodley or Wokingham.
card.voice: Calm, fairly flat and a bit clipped. He speaks fluent English with a noticeable but light Polish accent, and his word stress is occasionally slightly off. He answers the question asked and stops, without padding. He uses 'er' as a hesitation sometimes and a fair bit of 'sort of' and 'to be honest', picked up from years at work. He says 'dinner' for the evening meal and 'mate' with colleagues, and occasionally 'knackered'. He doesn't mind silence at all and will just wait. If a question is unclear he says 'sorry, what do you mean exactly?' rather than guessing.
card.typing: Proper capitals at the start of sentences and full stops, short sentences, mostly correct apostrophes. He rarely uses abbreviations other than 'e.g.' and 'etc'. He occasionally drops an article or uses a slightly odd preposition ('I am studying in second year'). He never uses emojis or exclamation marks.
card.with_strangers: Polite but reserved, and can come across as blunt or a little cold at first. He doesn't do much small talk and won't laugh at things he doesn't find funny. He is reliable and to the point, and he is clearly sceptical if something seems like a waste of time. He warms slightly if the conversation is practical.
small_things: His running time this week was 30 seconds slower because of the rain
The Oxford Road Polish shop has put prices up again
He needs to replace the brake pads on the Skoda
A group member hasn't done their part of the site report
He's been doing his reading at the library because the flat is cold
deeper_things: He worries that starting a degree at 31 means he is behind people his age
His father has a heart condition and he feels guilty being far away
He and Agnieszka are living mostly on her salary and it puts pressure on him
He sometimes feels neither fully Polish nor British any more
He goes to church more for his mother than for himself
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at slightly below eye level, framing his head and shoulders, with the light coming from a window to his left and a ceiling light on. He has a lean face, short dark-blond hair clipped at the sides and light stubble. His grey-blue eyes look directly at the camera, his mouth is neutral and slightly tight, and he is not smiling. He wears no glasses, and he has on a plain navy quarter-zip jumper over a white T-shirt collar. Behind him is a white wall with a large printed academic year planner pinned up, marked with coloured highlighter. A narrow pine bookshelf holds construction textbooks, a hard hat on the top shelf and a framed wedding photo. A small wooden crucifix hangs high on the wall to the right of the frame.
